rule_metadata.description: The dedicated module for Madd Silah, covering Lesser (Sughra) and Greater (Kubra) pronoun Haa' al-Kinayah lengthening rules and scholarly exceptions.

theoretical_foundation.linguistic_definition: Silah (صِلَة) means connection, linkage, or bridge.
theoretical_foundation.applied_tajweed_definition: Madd Silah applies to the third-person singular masculine pronoun of possession/reference (Haa' al-Kinayah - هـ) when it is vowelled and situated between two vowelled letters.

sub_divisions.sughra: Madd Silah Sughra (Lesser Connecting Madd): Pronoun is followed by any letter *except* Hamzah. Lengthened for **2 counts** (acting like Madd Tabii). Example: لَهُ مَا (Lahuu ma).
sub_divisions.kubra: Madd Silah Kubra (Greater Connecting Madd): Pronoun is followed immediately by a Hamzah (ء). Lengthened for **4 to 5 counts** (matching separated lengthening). Example: بِهِ إِلَّا (Bihii illaa).

theoretical_foundation.scholar_exception: In Surah Al-Furqan (verse 69), وَيَخْلُدْ فِيهِ مُهَانًا, the Haa is vowelled between two vowelled letters, yet Hafs recites it *without* Silah (short 1 count) due to specific transmission rules.
theoretical_foundation.wasl_vs_waqf: Silah applies strictly when connecting words in recitation (Wasl). If you pause (Waqf) on the pronoun word, the Silah drops entirely and the Haa is pronounced as a vowelless Sakinah (هْ).

practical_examples.breakdown: Haa pronoun of Lahu is between two vowels and followed by Meem; stretched 2 counts.
Haa pronoun of Bihi is followed by Hamzah; stretched 4 to 5 counts.
Haa is between vowels but recited without Silah (short 1 count) per Hafs narration.
